title: ISSP Overruns Nigerien Military Bases at Inatès and Banibangou, Tillabéri Region — Dozens of Soldiers Killed (June 17, 2026)
detail:
Islamic State Sahel Province (ISSP/ISGS) launched simultaneous, complex assaults on Nigerien Armed Forces (FAN) forward operating bases at Inatès and Banibangou in Tillabéri Region, near the Mali-Niger border, on June 17, 2026 — two of the last forward positions guarding against jihadist infiltration from Mali. Both bases were overrun in coordinated dawn attacks combining vehicle-borne assault teams, mortars, and small arms.

CASUALTY FIGURES (CONTESTED):
• Nigerien/international press consensus: at least 51 soldiers killed at Inatès, 34 at Banibangou (85 total)
• ISSP's own June 24 claim: 70 killed at Inatès, 10 at Banibangou (80 total)
• Nigerien opposition/exile sources: 101 at Inatès, 107 at Banibangou (208 total) — alleging the junta is suppressing the real toll

The wide range reflects both the chaos of two simultaneous overrun bases and what regional analysts describe as active suppression of casualty figures by Niger's military government. The attacks came 24 hours before a follow-on JNIM assault on Niamey's international airport (June 18), representing a 48-hour window in which Niger's security forces absorbed some of the heaviest losses of the insurgency to date.

The twin-base attacks underscore the deepening ISSP-JNIM rivalry playing out across Niger's southwest — both groups are competing for territorial and recruitment dominance in the Tillabéri-Dosso corridor, with each claiming larger, more spectacular operations to outbid the other.
